# Evidence
- Problem class: typescript-dist-missing-cjs-bridge-assets
- Model: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash
- Solved: 2026-09-27T23:36:29.500Z
- Verification: solution produced by pi in sandbox; see signatures.json

signatures.description: TypeScript pnpm monorepo (apps/server): three hand-written plain-CommonJS modules under src/services (legacy-bridge.js, legacy-usage-collector.js, server-game-engine.js) are spawned at runtime via path.resolve(__dirname, '<file>.js'), but tsconfig has no allowJs and the build is bare `tsc`, so dist/ never receives them. Under tsx (dev) and the docker CMD the src/ path resolves and masks the defect; only `node dist/index.js` (the shipped start script) dies with `Cannot find module .../dist/services/legacy-bridge.js` on every game, and because the child dies at require() before publishing any terminal event, the parent leaves the run RUNNING forever (its terminal predicate only checks completed_at). WORKING FIX: (1) append a tiny node copy step to the build script (`tsc && node scripts/copy-legacy-services.mjs`) that copies the known .js list from src/services to dist/services — allowJs was avoided to keep tsc emit semantics unchanged; prove with a forced non-cached build. (2) attach a child.on('close') handler where the spawn happens: on nonzero exit with no terminal evidence on the row, set the row's error column and call the run-completion check; extend that check (and the restart reconcile) to treat error!=null as terminal and mark the run FAILED. Covers both the missing-asset crash and the stuck-RUNNING invisibility. Verified: forced build re-emits all 3 files; prod-start 2-model benchmark run reaches COMPLETED with 0 MODULE_NOT_FOUND lines; unit test mocks child_process.spawn to prove the errored-row + FAILED-run path.
